title: Eid al-Fitr
hookLine: new clothes, the Eid prayer, visiting, sweets, and eid mubarak
last: ZAKAT AL-FITR — EVERYONE EATS ON EID.

lines: CLOTHES WITH THE TAGS STILL ON.
cards: It's early morning, and the house smells like cardamom and fried dough. Kids are up early, in clothes that still have the tags on. Someone eats a few dates standing in the kitchen.
On the way out, the family says it together, over and over: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar. In a park, a stadium, a big hall, thousands of people in their brightest colors line up in rows on the grass.
After a month of empty afternoons, today no one is allowed to fast.

teach.b: Eid means a festival. Arabic dictionaries tie it to a root for returning: the day that comes back every year.
Eid al-Fitr, the feast of breaking the fast, is the first day of the month after Ramadan, and much of it traces back to the Prophet ﷺ.
Anas said in Bukhari that the Prophet wouldn't go out on Eid morning until he'd eaten some dates, an odd number of them. The fast is broken first thing, on purpose: fasting on Eid is forbidden.
People wash, put on their best clothes, and go out to the Eid prayer, saying takbir along the way. The prayer is two rak'ahs, with extra takbirs, then a sermon.
The Prophet would go by one road and come back by another; scholars give several reasons, and one is that more people along the way could greet him.
Then the visiting, the food, the gifts for children, and the greetings: eid mubarak, a blessed Eid, and an older one reported from the companions, may Allah accept from us and from you.
A small story in Bukhari shows what the day is for. On an Eid, the Prophet was resting at home while two girls were singing. Abu Bakr came in and scolded them: this, in the Prophet's house?
The Prophet said: leave them, Abu Bakr.
Every people has its festival, and this is our festival. Some readers take this to mean the joy isn't a lapse after the serious month, but part of the worship.
And if, the week after, the prayers that came easily in Ramadan feel heavy again, that dip is common; day one hundred fifteen gave it a name. The door doesn't close with the month.

how: On Eid al-Fitr, Muslims eat a few dates, wear their best clothes, say takbir on the way to the Eid prayer in a mosque or open ground, listen to the sermon, then spend the day visiting family and friends, sharing food and gifts, and greeting each other with eid mubarak.

o: a greeting, from a root for meeting
the sermon given after the Friday prayer
a festival, from a root for returning

games.q: what's inside the feast — tap the pairs.

s: you can fast on the day of Eid to stretch Ramadan a little longer
fasting on the day of Eid is forbidden; the Prophet ﷺ ate dates before going out.
the Prophet told Abu Bakr to let the girls keep singing on Eid
every people has its festival, and this is our festival (Bukhari).
Eid al-Fitr falls on the same date every year
it's the first day of the month after Ramadan, so it moves with the moon.

games.q: you're Abu Bakr. it's Eid, and you walk into the Prophet's ﷺ house to find two girls singing. you scold them. what does the Prophet say?
o: you're right, this isn't the place
leave them; every people has its festival, and this is ours
let them finish this song, then stop
games.why: he told Abu Bakr to leave them: every people has its festival, and this is our festival (Bukhari).

practice: Think back over the month: the moon, the dawn meal, the date at sunset, the nights, the tongue, the gift.
Then think of one person to greet: if they're Muslim and it's Eid, eid mubarak; if not, or if it isn't Eid, a few words saying you're glad they exist. Let it be a small feast.

wordCard.voice: Eid. The festival that returns; Eid al-Fitr, the feast of breaking the fast, with dates, the prayer, visiting and sweets. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a blessed Eid. 'id is a festival, from a root for returning.

carryVoice: Your line: a blessed feast. Every people has its festival, and this is ours. See you tomorrow.
